target.title: fix(agents): keep bundle LSP tool names provider-safe
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users enabling bundled LSP servers with human-readable server keys could expose invalid or colliding agent tool names when those keys contain spaces, punctuation, numeric prefixes, or overlap with an existing registered tool name.

## Why This Change Was Made

The bundle LSP runtime now keeps the original server key for user-facing labels and execution details while deriving a provider-safe model-facing tool prefix for hover, definition, and references tools. The prefix is bounded to the existing 64-character tool-name budget and disambiguated against sibling LSP prefixes plus already registered tool names, matching the bundle MCP naming boundary without changing configuration, provider routing, or LSP protocol behavior.

## User Impact

Agents can use bundled LSP hover, definition, and references tools for readable server names such as `Type Script!` or numeric keys, and LSP tools are no longer dropped when the sanitized name would collide with a registered tool.

## Evidence

- Claim proved: at current head `25663d924f98daa0e22337a0b6ecdd6cc650952f`, bundled LSP tool materialization produces provider-safe, unique tool names from unsafe and colliding server keys, avoids a registered tool-name collision, spawns real stdio LSP child processes, and preserves the original server label in tool execution details.
- Focused regression: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/agent-bundle-lsp-runtime.test.ts` passed with 1 file and 10 tests.
- Real runtime transcript: `node --import tsx --input-type=module -` ran a repo-local script through `loadEmbeddedAgentLspConfig -> loadEnabledBundleLspConfig -> createBundleLspToolRuntime -> spawn child stdio LSP process -> initialize -> tool materialization -> hover execute` using an enabled file-backed Claude bundle with server keys `Type Script!`, `123`, and `Type-Script-`, plus reserved tool name `lsp_hover_Type-Script-`.

```json
{
  "head": "25663d924f98daa0e22337a0b6ecdd6cc650952f",
  "childProcessProof": {
    "commandBasename": "node.exe",
    "initializedServers": ["123", "Type Script!", "Type-Script-"],
    "hoverServer": "Type Script!",
    "distinctChildPids": 3
  },
  "toolNames": [
    "lsp_definition_Type-Script--2",
    "lsp_definition_Type-Script--3",
    "lsp_definition_lsp-123",
    "lsp_hover_Type-Script--2",
    "lsp_hover_Type-Script--3",
    "lsp_hover_lsp-123",
    "lsp_references_Type-Script--2",
    "lsp_references_Type-Script--3",
    "lsp_references_lsp-123"
  ],
  "checks": {
    "allProviderSafe": true,
    "allLengthOk": true,
    "unique": true
  },
  "hoverResult": {
    "toolName": "lsp_hover_Type-Script--2",
    "details": {
      "lspServer": "Type Script!",
      "lspMethod": "hover"
    },
    "textIncludesOriginalServer": true
  }
}
```

- Targeted format: `node_modules\.bin\oxfmt.CMD --check --threads=1 src\agents\agent-bundle-lsp-runtime.ts src\agents\agent-bundle-lsp-runtime.test.ts` passed.
- Committed diff hygiene: `git diff --check HEAD~1..HEAD` passed.
- Review proof: `python .agents\skills\autoreview\scripts\autoreview --mode commit --commit HEAD` completed with no accepted/actionable findings.
- Duplicate search: no open self PR with the same root cause; `bundle LSP tool name` and `lsp_hover` open PR searches were empty, and `agent-bundle-lsp-runtime` only found adjacent LSP lifecycle/size PRs rather than a tool-name fix.

AI-assisted: yes. I reviewed the bundle LSP runtime path, sibling bundle MCP naming helper, and focused regression coverage.
